title: Microburst PR strategy and smoke checklist
content:
Purpose:
Quick, focused set of heuristics and a tiny checklist for shipping micro-PRs (<= 200 LOC, single logical change). Notes-to-self style — intended to be copied into PR descriptions or used during 5–10m reviews.

Context / why this matters:
- We keep getting stalled on medium-sized PRs where multiple concerns (perf, correctness, style, infra) are mixed.
- Microbursts: aim to split change into a small, testable change that can be reviewed and rolled back quickly.
- This doc collects practical checks so reviewers have consistent expectations and authors can self-audit before request.

Quick decision rubric (author):
1) Can I explain the change in one sentence? If not, refactor/focus.
2) Does the change touch more than one subsystem (runtime, build, infra)? If yes, split.
3) Is there a small smoke test I can add that fails before and passes after? If no, add one or mark as "needs-integration".

Reviewer fast-pass checklist (5–7 mins):
- Scope: Does title + description match changes? (files + intent)
- Tests: Are there unit/smoke tests? Do they actually exercise the change (not just imports)?
- Safety: Any new config/feature flags? Is default behavior unchanged?
- Backwards compatibility: Are wire formats/schema changes guarded or versioned?
- Perf regressions: Any new allocations/loops in hot path? Quick fingerprint: grep for buffers, memcpy, vector->reserve, allocations in critical path.
- Logging/metrics: New errors should map to existing spans/metrics; avoid spamming ERROR for recoverable cases.

Extra checks for serving-runtime PRs (perf-sensitive):
- KV cache: does this change affect cache keys or prefix behavior? If yes, include migration notes.
- Batching: ensure batch size calculations unchanged; add microbenchmark snapshot if touching batching code.
- Quantization path: code paths for int8/4 should be exercised by tests or flagged.
- Kernel selection: changes touching kernel lookup should include a fallback test for missing kernel (simulate with env var).

Smoke test examples (copyable):
- python -m smoke_tests.smoke_infer --model small-gpt --seq 64 --requests 5 --concurrency 2
  Expected: no OOM, latency p95 < 2s, 200/200 OK
- curl -sS -X POST $REDWOOD_API/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' | jq .choices[0].text
  Quick sanity: not an empty string, no stack traces in body

PR description template (one-paragraph):
- What: single sentence summary.
- Why: 1–2 line motivation + user-visible impact (perf, bugfix, toil reduction).
- Risk: short list (backwards breaking? flags?).
- Test plan: exact commands and expected outputs.
- Rollout: feature flag + canary details if applicable.

Notes to self: common micro-PR anti-patterns to avoid:
- Sneaking unrelated formatting or dependency bumps into a behavior change PR.
- Adding telemetry in a separate commit but combined in one PR (makes revert harder).
- Large config surface changes without default-preserving behavior.

Follow-ups (if approved):
- INF-2741: add compact benchmark harness for quant path (deadline: next sprint).
- Convert flaky integration check into a deterministic unit test (Diego to pair).
- Add PR template snippet to repo README so authors copy the smoke-test commands.

Unresolved / questions:
- How aggressive should we be about requiring microbench snapshots for any PR touching batching? (tradeoff: reviewer overhead vs catching regressions)
- Should we auto-run the smoke commands as part of a pre-merge bot for PRs tagged "microburst"?

One-off heuristics I've used (keep as quick mental checklist):
- If a reviewer needs to run >3 manual commands to verify correctness, split.
- If the change alters a single function signature and the compiler fails in multiple modules, prefer a thin adapter PR first.
- Favor feature-flagged changes even within micro-PRs for runtime-affecting changes.

Recent example notes (from local workflow):
- PR #1428: split perf counter delta into separate commit. Adding the smoke test caught a regression in p95 (missed small allocation). Reverted allocation commit and landed the logic-only change.
- Slack thread #runtime-review 2025-01-15: Diego suggested adding a fallback env var for kernel lookup — do this whenever touching kernel selection.

Checklist before marking PR "ready for review":
- [ ] Title + one-sentence summary
- [ ] Added smoke test + instructions in PR body
- [ ] Verified no default-behavior regressions locally (run smoke commands)
- [ ] Added feature flag if change touches request routing / model selection
- [ ] Linked related JIRA/issue keys

Copy this into PR descriptions and tweak as needed. If reviewers want, we can make a tiny GitHub action to run the two smoke commands above for any PR with label "microburst".

End notes: keep it low friction — the goal is faster, safer merges, not bureaucracy. If in doubt, ping Diego or leave a short "needs-pair-review" note in the PR and ship the behavioral change separately from cleanup/refactors.
